transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I guess… what finally scared me into coming is I keep having this thought that it would be a relief if I just didn’t wake up. I haven’t tried to hurt myself or anything like that, but the thought keeps coming around.

I was sitting at home thinking about it, and then I started worrying about whether that’s a normal thing people my age think about, or if I’m just being dramatic… I don’t know. It frightened me enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
How long have you been feeling this way, with these thoughts of not wanting to wake up?

Um… I think it’s been about four months now. It kind of started after my aunt came to live with us. I remember because we were moving some of her boxes around, and she has so many old things, you know, dishes wrapped in newspaper and all that… but yes, around then. About four months.
Over the past four months, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends?

Yes… I have. I used to really look forward to doing my watercolors, and there’s a dance class I’d go to, and I’d walk with some ladies, you know, around the neighborhood. One of them always talks about her roses, and I used to like hearing about that…

But lately I just leave my paints sitting there. The paper and everything is out, but I don’t touch it. I don’t go to class. I can’t seem to make myself care about any of it, even though I know I used to.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the past four months?

I… I’m not really sure. I don’t keep track of my weight much. My daughter has one of those scales in the bathroom, but I mostly just push it out of the way when I’m cleaning.

As for eating, some days I just make toast or something simple, but I couldn’t tell you if that’s different enough to count. I’ve always been a picky eater anyway—my aunt says I never liked proper meals, even when I was younger. So… I don’t know that I’ve noticed a real change.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes… most mornings, I think. I wake up and there’s this heavy sadness right here in my chest, like I’ve already failed the whole day before I even get out of bed.

Sometimes I just lie there listening to the house sounds—my aunt moves around so early, she’s always clinking something in the kitchen—and I think, “Well, here we go again.” It’s not always loud, if that makes sense, but it’s there most of the day.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or have you felt restless or unable to sit still?

I think… slower, yes. My husband says I move like everything takes extra effort now, like I’m walking through syrup or something. He’ll say, “You’re still getting your shoes on?” and I don’t even realize I’ve been sitting there that long.

Even at the market, I’ll go in for one thing—milk, or those little oranges my aunt likes, though she always says the skins are too thick—and I’ll just stand there in front of the shelf too long before I pick up what I came for. I don’t feel so much restless, more like I’m… stuck.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling like you’re not worth much?

Yes… I do, I think. Mostly about my aunt. She’s been family all my life, and she’ll ask for something or make a comment, and I’ll feel tired or irritated, and then right away I think, what kind of woman gets annoyed at her own aunt?

It makes me feel like I’m bad… like I’m not grateful enough. My mother used to say you don’t bring shame on the family, you keep things respectful, and I’ll hear that in my head sometimes. Even if I don’t say anything out loud, just feeling that way makes me feel ashamed.
Have you noticed that you’ve been feeling more tired or that you’re losing energy easily, even when you’re not doing much?

Yes… I get tired so easy now. Even if I’ve been in bed all night, when I get up my body feels like it already did a day’s work.

Like carrying a basket of laundry, or just making breakfast—toast, eggs, nothing fancy—it takes more out of me than it should. And then I’ll sit down “just for a minute,” and next thing I know I’m still sitting there, looking at the table or thinking I should wipe the counter… My aunt likes the counter wiped a certain way, she always notices crumbs. But yes, it’s the tiredness. It’s there even when I haven’t done much.
Have you had any thoughts about how you would end your life, or have you thought about making a plan for not waking up?

I… I haven’t made a plan like that, no. I haven’t tried to hurt myself.

But what scared me—what made me think I needed to come in—is I keep having this thought that it would be a relief if I just didn’t wake up. Like if I went to sleep and that was it. And then I think about my aunt needing her tea in the morning, or how she complains if the kettle tastes funny, and I feel awful even saying it… but yes, that thought keeps coming back.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating on things, like following a recipe, reading, or making decisions?

I don’t know… I mean, I can follow some things if they’re simple. I don’t read much anyway, never was one for sitting with books like my cousin used to—she could read those thick paperbacks all afternoon.

Recipes… I mostly cook things I already know, so I’m not sure. If it’s something written down with too many steps, I might just not bother. But I don’t know if that’s concentrating or just me being tired of fussing with it. Decisions, well… I’ve never liked making big decisions. My aunt always has an opinion about how things should be done, so sometimes it’s easier to just do it her way.
Over the past month, have these feelings of sadness, low energy, and loss of interest interfered with your ability to carry out your usual responsibilities at home or with family?

Yes… I mean, not like the house is falling apart, but I’m not keeping up like I used to.

I stopped going to my dance class, and that walking group I used to do—well, I kept telling myself I’d go next week, and then next week came and I just… didn’t. I used to help at the food pantry too, just a little shift, nothing important like the ladies who run the whole thing, but I haven’t been going.

And my husband’s been doing more errands now because I get started and then I get stuck, or I’m late, or I forget where I was in the middle of it. He’ll say, “I’ll just go,” and I let him, even though I feel bad about it. So yes, it has gotten in the way.
Have you found it difficult to do things that you needed to do at home or work, even when you tried your best, because of your low mood or lack of energy?

Yes… yes, I think so. I try, I really do, but I just don’t seem to keep up the way I used to.

Like I’ve stopped going to my dance class, and the walking group too—those ladies probably think I’m just being rude, though one of them always wore those bright purple sneakers, you could see her coming a mile away. And the food pantry shifts… I haven’t been going in like I should.

At home, my husband’s been taking over more errands because I’ll start to do something and then I get stuck, or I fall behind, and then he just says he’ll handle it. I feel bad letting him, but it’s like I can’t get myself moving right.
